text:
maria: quick heads-up — ran a microbench of the paged-attn prefetch scheduler against a 70/30 chat/text mix. results look odd: tail latency spikes when prefetch.window > 3.

alex: can you paste the config you used? was this on flashv2 or the new flashv3 path?

maria: flashv3 path. config snippet: ```
prefetch.window = 5
prefetch.batch_coalesce = true
scheduler.policy = latency_prefetch
kv.page_size = 64KB
kv.max_prefetch_inflight = 8
```

todd: hmm, we recently changed block_table.handoff to eagerly pin one extra block per slotmap entry. could that increase memory pressure and cause async io stalls? :thinking: 

maria: plausible. memory used looked fine overall, but we saw a burst of dev/blk io waits correlated with p95->p99. attaching timeline excerpt.

jen: timeline + flame is helpful. did you capture kernel selection traces? maybe it fell back to fused kernel under certain seq_len distributions.

maria: yes, captured traces. interesting bit: when prefetch.window=5 we see more kernel-choice flips from flashv3_fused -> fallback_flash_compat at ~1200ms mark. with window=3 flips are almost absent. so probably prefetch created more inflight KV pages, changing seq len distribution and triggering kernel heuristics.

perf-bot: benchmark summary (run id a8f3): model=redwood-13b-like, batch-mix=single-turn chatheavy, tokens/sampled=1M, p50=40ms, p95=180ms (w=3), p95=420ms (w=5), p99=820ms (w=5). trace and perf counters uploaded to s3://redwood-perf/3812345670/a8f3/

alex: okay that explains latency but why kernel flips? our kernel chooser threshold is based on avg_seq_len + inflight_kv_pages heuristics. if prefetch inflates effective seq_len estimate, the chooser might select a kernel with worse cold-cache performance.

maria: agree. i instrumented the chooser: when inflight_kv_pages > 6 chooser sets prefer_fused=false. with window=5 that hits frequently.

jen: two levers to try: 1) decouple kernel choice from inflight_kv_pages and instead use observed active_seq_len (exclude prefetched pages not yet hit) or 2) cap max_prefetch_inflight down for chat-heavy mixes.

alex: i prefer #1 long-term. heuristics should be based on actual seq_len distribution, not prefetch speculative state. #2 is quick mitigation.

maria: tried #2: set max_prefetch_inflight=4 + prefetch.window=5 -> p95 dropped back to ~210ms, p99 ~360ms. much better.

perf-bot: note added to run id a8f3: mitigation applied -> max_prefetch_inflight=4.

ci-bot: perf regression alert created: PR 8123 links to bench runs and traces.

todd: we still need root cause on allocator side. when prefetch inflight grows, block-table churn increases and we saw more slab splits in the hot arena which increases CPU jitter. i can add counters to block_table for split_count and slot_reallocs.

maria: yes please. also can we log kernel-chooser decision reasons in trace spans? that would make correlation easier.

jen: adding both items to my todo. i'll do chooser span + block_table counters. i suspect a small tweak: when prefetch is speculative, flag pages as 'prefetch' and exclude them from kernel heuristics.

alex: one more thought: batching heuristics. with prefetch.coalesce we saw larger fused batches which are good for throughput but worse for tail. maybe add a soft cap on coalesced batch-size when any inflight_prefetch exists.

maria: good point — we trade tail for throughput. i'll run a matrix: window={2,3,5}, max_prefetch_inflight={2,4,8}, coalesce={on,off} and collect p50/p95/p99 + kernel-flip counts.

perf-bot: scheduled large sweep: job id sweep-381234 on canary fleet, 24h. will post results in this thread.

jen: thanks — once we have block_table counters + chooser spans we can correlate split_count -> kernel-flip -> p99. hopefully a small heuristic fix will clear this without sacrificing throughput. :thumbsup:

maria: Thanks all. i'll add the first artifacts to s3 and tag the CI PR once the sweep completes.

alex: nice work. keep the mitigations in a hotfix branch until we land chooser changes.

maria: yup, creating hotfix/381234-prefetch-cap now.

perf-bot: sweep started: sweep-381234. results will be posted as they complete.
